articles.title: Apple Has a Software Problem + Nvidia’s CEO Crisis with Joanna Stern
articles.content: In this episode of Power On, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman is joined by technology journalist and reviewer Joanna Stern of The New Things and NBC News for a critical look at Apple’s software leadership and its struggles to compete in artificial intelligence. They discuss whether software chief Craig Federighi’s management style and Apple’s rigid development processes are holding the company back, why Siri continues to fail at basic tasks and whether Apple needs to start over with a new AI assistant. They also examine how Apple’s AI shortcomings have delayed major hardware products. Plus, their experiences with the iPhone Duo, its new face-unlock feature, Joanna’s HomeView review and whether Apple’s Johny Srouji could be a candidate to lead Nvidia following its leadership crisis. Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.content: Anthropic shares are set to soar when they start trading on Thursday, after the artificial intelligence lab’s $107.3 billion IPO and private placement broke SpaceX’s record for the biggest-ever offering. Anthropic’s debut shifts the spotlight in the AI investment boom from companies making the tools to run the most advanced models to the model makers themselves. With hundreds of billions of dollars committed to infrastructure such as chips and data centers, the next test for the top AI labs is to grow revenue fast enough to outpace the industry’s ambitious spending plans. articles.title: Anthropic 完成史上最大规模 IPO，上市估值达 1.5 万亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，北京时间今天（19 日）深夜，AI 初创企业 Anthropic 正式登陆美股，以 813 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 5,431.47 亿元人民币）的募资额创下 IPO 历史纪录。公司 CEO 达里奥 · 阿莫代伊在纳斯达克敲响开市钟。“今天的上市让公司的财务基础更加稳固，也让我们更加坚定了做正确事情的决心。”Anthropic 的发行价定为每股 83 美元（现汇率约合 554.5 元人民币），高于上周公布的预期区间，完全稀释后市值达到 1.5 万亿美元（现汇率约合 10.02 万亿元人民币）。彭博社和路透社报道称，预计正式开盘后，Anthropic 股价还将上涨约 20%，达到每股 100 美元（现汇率约合 668.1 元人民币）左右。当地时间 18 日，Anthropic 还宣布向承销商出售 9.8 亿股股票，扩大后的发行规模使募资总额达到 813 亿美元（现汇率约合 5,431.47 亿元人民币），打破 SpaceX 今年 6 月 IPO 募资 750 亿美元（现汇率约合 5,010.58 亿元人民币）的纪录。Anthropic 成立于 2021 年，仅用了五年左右的时间，便有望跻身全球市值最高的上市公司之列。Anthropic 是首家上市的前沿 AI 研发机构，其股价表现将成为观察数万亿美元 AI 投资热潮的重要风向标。华尔街投资者和全球科技行业都在密切关注公司上市后的表现。Anthropic 于 10 月底提交的招股书显示，公司成立以来每年营收都呈爆发式增长，部分年份增幅甚至超过 1000%。2026 年上半年，Anthropic 营收达到 162 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,082.29 亿元人民币），远高于 2025 年全年的 46 亿美元（现汇率约合 307.32 亿元人民币）。但 Anthropic 也付出了巨大的财务代价。公司 2026 年上半年亏损 800 亿美元（现汇率约合 5,344.62 亿元人民币），主要源于一笔一次性费用，前九个月累计亏损进一步扩大至 1,040 亿美元（现汇率约合 6,948.01 亿元人民币）。随着 Anthropic 不断扩大算力资源投入，成本预计还会大幅攀升。算力主要由通常部署在数据中心的半导体芯片提供，是运行生成式 AI 的基础，也是 Anthropic 最大的支出项目。2026 年前九个月，公司在算力方面花费约 188 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,255.99 亿元人民币）。Anthropic 高管在招股书中写道：“开发前沿 AI 模型需要投入大量算力、资金和人力，开展可能持续数周甚至数月的大规模训练，每次训练的费用可能高达数百万美元。”Anthropic 还在招股文件中详细披露了旗下 AI 模型可能给人类带来的各种风险，包括被用于开发生物武器，或加剧世界各地的压迫行为。此前，员工曾担忧部分企业以不负责任的方式开发先进 AI 模型，阿莫代伊随后呼吁放缓最先进 AI 模型的研发速度。

articles.title: 《GTA 6》藏有两个“简单模式”开关：降低敌人血量、减少车辆受损
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，此前有消息称，《GTA 6》在玩家通关主线剧情之前无法使用作弊码。不仅如此，启用作弊码还会锁定剧情进度，并关闭游戏存档功能。这意味着，玩家只能通过作弊码短暂体验一番疯狂犯罪的乐趣，随后就必须回归正常游戏流程。这一改动让部分玩家颇有微词。不过，对于希望降低游戏难度、又不想偏离开发团队原本设计体验的玩家来说，还有一个好消息：《GTA 6》实际上提供了两个设置，可以让游戏变得更加容易。据IT之家了解，玩家只需打开游戏设置菜单，进入“Gameplay”（游戏玩法）选项，就能找到“Accessible Combat”（无障碍战斗）和“Reduced Vehicle Damage”（降低车辆损伤）两个开关。开启这两项功能后，游戏中一些难度较高的环节就会变得容易应对。其中，“无障碍战斗”会降低敌人的生命值，同时减少敌人对玩家角色造成的伤害，效果类似传统游戏中的难度调节选项。“降低车辆损伤”则会减少玩家车辆受到的伤害，让车辆拥有更强的耐久能力。这项设置适用于枪击、环境因素以及碰撞造成的损伤。不过，Rockstar 对启用这两项设置的玩家也给出了提醒。游戏会弹出提示，称这些调整将“显著改变游戏的平衡性和体验”。经过实际体验可以发现，这两项设置虽然远称不上真正的“无敌模式”，但开启后确实能明显降低游戏难度。杰森和露西亚在遭受近战攻击或枪击时能够承受更多伤害。即使驾驶杰森那辆破旧不堪的皮卡，也需要刻意制造碰撞，才能让车辆达到轻微冒烟的受损状态。当然，实际效果可能因玩家的游戏方式而有所不同，但就目前的体验来看，这两项设置确实能够让《GTA 6》变得更加容易。考虑到使用作弊码会导致成就解锁和游戏进度受到限制，如果玩家希望更顺利地体验主线剧情，不妨考虑启用这两项设置。除了上述两项功能，游戏还提供了另外 23 项游戏玩法无障碍选项、12 项显示选项、70 项用户界面选项、24 项摄像机选项以及 14 项音频选项。Rockstar 用户界面副总监萨姆 · 格罗塞特（Sam Grosset）此前在向 Eurogamer 提供的资料中表示：“我们致力于为每一位玩家打造包容、直观且沉浸感十足的游戏体验。无障碍设计从开发之初就已纳入考虑范围，为不同需求的玩家进行设计，也能帮助我们为所有人打造更好的游戏。”他还表示，团队希望《GTA 6》中的每位玩家都能按照自己的喜好体验游戏。无论是选择更大的字体、采用更简洁的屏幕显示方式，还是调整冲刺操作的控制方式，玩家都可以根据自身需求进行选择。此外，Rockstar 此前还透露，《GTA 6》的任务设计变得更加开放，玩家有更多机会按照自己的方式完成目标，任务也因此变得“更难失败”。游戏还支持多个存档文件以及任务重玩功能。

articles.title: 吴泳铭：阿里“2032 年全球数据中心规模超 20GW”目标或下调
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据蓝鲸新闻报道，在阿里巴巴今天（19 日）召开的 2027 财年第二季度业绩电话会上，阿里巴巴集团 CEO 吴泳铭表示，全球各个区域的算力政策出现了非常大的变化，将对阿里云的数据中心建设产生影响。吴泳铭透露，根据目前的初步评估，阿里此前制定的到 2032 年全球数据中心规模超过 20GW 的目标有可能下调，资本开支可能有一定程度降低。同时，阿里将在国产算力及相关供应链上投入更积极，推进整体计划。基于平头哥的算力供应链持续放量节奏，2027 年和 2028 年上半年将是阿里最大的一个持续投资阶段。吴泳铭另表示，对于长期的现金流规划非常有信心。据IT之家此前报道，吴泳铭表示，2027 年和 2028 年，将是中国算力最紧缺的两年。2027 年以后，阿里云的芯片供给都会以国产平头哥芯片为主，同时也会采购其他国产芯片来支持内部的推理需求。相关阅读：《阿里巴巴 CEO 吴泳铭：2027、2028 年将是中国算力最紧缺的两年》

articles.title: R 星联合创始人谈《GTA》系列为何不用真实车型：授权成本、创作自由等因素
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，随着《GTA 6》正式开启全球发售，不少玩家和业内人士又提出了一个老问题：R 星为何至今不肯在游戏中使用真实的汽车品牌和车型？《GTA 5》发售前三天就赚了 10 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 66.81 亿元人民币），《GTA 6》的预购金额更是超过 15 亿美元（现汇率约合 100.21 亿元人民币），按理来说，成本似乎不是问题。不过，坚持使用虚构品牌并不只是为了节省成本。R 星联合创始人杰米 · 金在接受 Killaz 采访时解释，获得汽车品牌授权不仅费用高昂，双方还需要投入大量时间和精力。另一个原因是 R 星希望保留创作自由。杰米 · 金透露，公司希望尽可能使用原创内容，不愿在游戏开发中受制于其他企业。GTA 系列向来以讽刺美国社会著称，引入真实汽车品牌可能破坏游戏原有的风格。此外，愿意让旗下车型出现在《GTA 6》中的车企恐怕也寥寥无几。汽车厂商一向十分重视品牌形象，每年不惜投入数亿美元甚至数十亿美元，通过精心设计的营销活动宣传旗下车型。例如，如果本田授权 GTA 系列使用旗下车型，玩家就能驾驶 CR-V 和奥德赛持枪抢劫、撞倒无辜路人，显然不是本田希望自己的品牌呈现出的形象。而在游戏中，不少载具本来就与现实车型十分相似。例如，游戏中的“艳妇 D10”“泰皮斯达”和“艾梅鲁斯”，分别借鉴了雪佛兰科尔维特、兰博基尼 Huracán 和迈凯伦塞纳的设计。

articles.title: 微软官方 PyPI 包 Agent Framework 遭劫持，攻击者植入窃取登录凭据的恶意软件
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据科技媒体 TechRadar 今天报道，微软官方在 PyPI 发布的 Agent Framework 软件包遭黑客劫持，攻击者将其植入窃取登录凭据和云平台令牌的恶意软件。但幸运的是，被植入恶意软件的版本仅存在 31 分钟就被删除。IT之家了解到，微软 Agent Framework Python 是一款开源工具包，每月下载量已接近 20 万次，可帮助开发者构建 AI 智能体，使其能够调用工具、遵循指令、与其他智能体交互，并执行更加复杂的任务。11 月 17 日，黑客将 Agent Framework 劫持并发布 1.26.1 版本，其中的恶意软件会在 Python 启动时自动执行，即使运行环境并未导入 Agent Framework 软件包也不例外。同时，该软件包旨在窃取 Azure、AWS、GitHub、Docker、Hugging Face、OpenAI 等服务的登录凭据，并获取本地配置文件和其他进程的信息。PyPI 仅用 31 分钟就发现了此次入侵，并隔离了恶意版本。但两分钟以后，第二次攻击（1.26.2）接踵而至。新软件增加了 GitHub Actions OIDC 令牌请求功能，还能够自动搜索 GitHub Runner 目录，只不过发布 8 分钟后就被清除。目前，我们尚不清楚此次攻击是否导致开发者信息泄露。如果您曾下载过 1.26.1 或 1.26.2，请立即删除，并仔细检查系统是否存在可疑文件、撤销现有登录凭据、检查 Azure 或 AWS 等服务是否存在未授权访问。

articles.title: 瞒不住了：英国法院裁定政府必须承认曾要求苹果“开后门”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据英国《金融时报》报道，英国一家法院裁定，英国政府必须承认曾向苹果公司发出秘密命令，要求其允许政府访问用户的加密数据。这一裁决为英国内政部与这家科技巨头围绕隐私和数据安全问题的公开对峙铺平了道路。当地时间周四，英国调查权力法庭（Investigatory Powers Tribunal）驳回了内政部要求对相关行动保密的申请。此前，英国政府试图迫使苹果在其系统中建立一个被批评者称为“后门”的访问通道，以绕过保护用户数据的加密机制。法庭指出，内政部未能证明，公开苹果曾收到“技术能力通知”（Technical Capability Notice，TCN）一事会对国家安全造成损害。这意味着，与调查权力法庭审理的大多数案件不同，苹果及相关非营利组织针对英国政府的法律挑战，将有相当一部分内容可以在公开法庭上进行。参与此次法律行动的英国非营利组织 Privacy International 与 Liberty，此前也曾就英国政府发出的秘密命令向调查权力法庭提出申诉。Privacy International 的法律倡导人士将此次裁决称为“问责制、透明度和网络安全领域的一次重大胜利”。IT之家注意到，今年 7 月，苹果在收到英国政府发出的第二份技术能力通知后，再次对英国政府提起法律诉讼。此前一年，英国政府曾在与美国政府发生争议后，同意撤回此前的一项类似要求。技术能力通知依据英国《调查权力法案》发出。该法案禁止任何收到此类通知的机构承认命令的存在，也不允许其讨论相关内容。这类通知可以迫使企业向英国安全部门提供客户数据访问权限，即使这些数据受到强加密技术的保护，也可能被要求开放访问。不过，调查权力法庭周四指出，英国政府此前一直奉行对秘密命令“既不确认也不否认”（NCND）的政策，但有关技术能力通知的消息已经被媒体披露。此外，英国政府还曾在华盛顿与美国官员讨论此事。这些行为都构成了对原有保密政策的“重大偏离”。法庭在裁决中写道：“这些偏离‘既不确认也不否认’政策的行为累积起来，意味着任何对这一话题稍有关注的人，都已经知道内政部向苹果发出了一份技术能力通知。”法庭还认为，如果此时由政府正式确认该命令的存在，就会对国家安全造成损害，或者向“恶意行为者”提供新信息，这种说法已经显得不切实际。Privacy International 法律总监卡罗琳 · 威尔逊 · 帕洛（Caroline Wilson Palow）表示：“今天的裁决是透明度和有效监督方面的一次重大胜利。政府不应将‘既不确认也不否认’政策当作一道密不透风的屏障。”

articles.title: Audio Vivid 生态再进一步：理想汽车官宣上线菁彩声，支持声音对象精准空间定位与动态渲染
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，理想汽车官方今日宣布上线菁彩声 Audio Vivid。据介绍，在今日的 2026 声音设计创新大赛启动现场，理想汽车联合产业伙伴官宣菁彩声 Audio Vivid 车载功能上线。菁彩声 Audio Vivid 支持声音对象的精准空间定位与动态渲染，可让人声、乐器与环境音独立分布在不同方位、距离，声源位置随内容实时变化。目前理想车机端网易云音乐、汽水音乐、喜马拉雅均已上线 Audio Vivid 内容。IT之家注：菁彩声 Audio Vivid 是 UWA 联盟发布的三维声音频技术标准，是全球首个基于 AI 技术的音频编解码标准。该技术标准自 2022 年起已成功应用于总台春晚、奥运会、“九三阅兵”等大型活动直播。另外，国家标准化管理委员会去年 8 月 29 日批准发布了三项数字媒体领域关键技术国家标准，包括：《GB/T 46269.1-2025 高动态范围（HDR）视频技术第 1 部分：元数据及适配》《GB/T 46269.2-2025 高动态范围（HDR）视频技术第 2 部分：应用指南》《GB/T 46271-2025 信息技术三维声技术编码、分发与呈现》此次发布的三项标准由全国音频、视频及多媒体系统与设备标准化技术委员会（SAC / TC 242）等单位牵头起草，于 2025 年 8 月 29 日正式发布，并将于 2026 年 3 月 1 日起实施，将对广播电视、互联网视听、消费电子等多个行业产生影响。相关阅读：《菁彩影像 HDR Vivid、菁彩声 Audio Vivid 等三项国标发布》

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，国家知识产权局商标局最新信息显示，安徽江淮汽车集团股份有限公司近期申请注册了“帝境”商标，申请日期为 2025 年 11 月 19 日，目前处于“注册商标”阶段。该商标归属于国际分类第 12 类，涵盖的商品 / 服务范围包括：电动运载工具、汽车、混合动力汽车、卡车、电动汽车、自动驾驶汽车、汽车车身、汽车底盘、陆地车辆用电动机、汽车轮胎等。IT之家注意到，除了帝境之外，江淮汽车还注册了谛境、缔境等一批同音或近似的境字商标。据上海证券报报道，业内专家表示，帝境新商标与江淮、华为、玛莎拉蒂的未来合作关系密切。公开资料显示，尊界是华为与江淮汽车采用鸿蒙智行模式合作推出的豪华汽车品牌。2026 年也是尊界产品大年，6 月底尊界推出了 200 万元级旗舰车型，旗舰 MPV 双车 V800 / V680 则于 8 月上市。随着后续 SUV 车型的落地，尊界将形成“轿车 + MPV + SUV”完整产品矩阵，覆盖超豪华细分市场。

articles.title: Newzoo：《GTA 6》首周收入有望超《星球大战》《指环王》《哈利 · 波特》各自最卖座影片总和
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，千呼万唤始出来，《GTA 6》终于发售。按照游戏市场研究机构 Newzoo 的预测，R 星通过《GTA 6》首周获得的收入，有望超过《星球大战》《指环王》和《哈利 · 波特》系列各自最卖座电影的票房总和。Gearbox 负责人兰迪 · 皮奇福德在 X 平台发文称：“Newzoo 预测，《GTA 6》首周收入将超过《哈利 · 波特》《指环王》和《星球大战》系列票房最高的三部电影首轮上映票房的总和。”皮奇福德引用的应该是 Newzoo 今年 7 月发布的预测。当时，《GTA 6》刚刚开启预购，Newzoo 预计游戏发售首周的累计销售额可达 33 亿至 52 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 220.47 亿至 347.4 亿元人民币）。R 星还没有公布官方销量，《GTA 6》的开局表现相当亮眼。索尼和微软此前分别确认，《GTA 6》创下了各自数字商店的游戏预购量纪录。市场研究机构 Sensor Tower 估计，截至昨天，游戏累计售出 1707 万份，收入达到 16.5 亿美元（现汇率约合 110.23 亿元人民币）。根据 Box Office Mojo 的数据，《星球大战》《指环王》和《哈利 · 波特》系列票房最高的电影分别为《星球大战 7：原力觉醒》《指环王 3：王者无敌》和《哈利 · 波特与死亡圣器（下）》，全球累计票房分别约为 20.7 亿美元（现汇率约合 138.29 亿元人民币）、11.2 亿美元（现汇率约合 74.82 亿元人民币）和 13.4 亿美元（现汇率约合 89.52 亿元人民币），三部电影合计约 45.3 亿美元（现汇率约合 302.64 亿元人民币）。按照 Sensor Tower 的最新估算，《GTA 6》的收入距离 45.3 亿美元还有不小的差距。但游戏才刚刚发售，Newzoo 预测的则是整个首发周的成绩。如果最终达到预测区间的较高水平，《GTA 6》发售短短几天的收入，甚至可能比三部电影的票房总和多出 5 亿美元（现汇率约合 33.4 亿元人民币）以上，着实惊人。

articles.title: 谷歌与蓝色起源合作，计划 2029 年发射 AI 服务器卫星

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，如今的互联网早已与《GTA 5》发售时大不相同，这也是 Rockstar Games 没有在《GTA 6》中延续前作虚拟网站设计的原因之一。在《GTA 5》中，玩家可以访问 Lifeinvadder、Bleeter 和 Eyefind 等虚构网站，体验 Rockstar 对现实互联网的讽刺。而在《GTA 6》中，这些网站已经被 BuckMe、Scooter Bros 和 WhatUp 等手机应用取代。Rockstar 给出的理由很简单：智能手机应用更符合当下的使用习惯。Rockstar North 负责人罗布 · 纳尔逊（Rob Nelson）在接受《Kotaku》采访时表示：“我们觉得没有必要继续保留网站。我们确实希望将重点放在手机应用上，并围绕这些应用展开设计。”尽管《GTA 6》中的部分应用与前作虚拟网站的功能相似，但纳尔逊表示，开发团队不希望玩家因为盯着屏幕而忽略游戏中精心打造的开放世界。这一设计思路还涉及游戏的经济系统。Rockstar 希望玩家能够真正感受到金钱的价值，并见证杰森（Jason）和露西亚（Lucia）的成长历程：两人从抢劫当铺起步，逐渐发展到策划大型银行劫案。纳尔逊解释说：“他们并不需要通过网站购买大量东西，你明白我的意思吧？因此，游戏中的一切都能随着剧情自然发展。”他同时表示，未来不排除重新引入网站。IT之家注意到，纳尔逊还回忆了团队讨论是否保留网站时的一段经历。他曾向负责二维美术和用户界面的斯图 · 佩特里（Stu Petri）询问网站设计，对方反问：“为什么要做网站？你到底需要它来干什么？”这番话也让团队最终决定不再沿用前作的设计。Rockstar 此前向媒体提供的评测资料中，该工作室用户界面副总监萨姆 · 格罗塞特（Sam Grosset）也介绍了手机应用的设计思路。他表示，团队在应用的交互方式上下了很大功夫，力求让手机操作自然融入玩家的游戏习惯，尽可能发挥其作用。格罗塞特表示：“我们确保用户界面能够成为游戏世界的自然延伸，在不打断游戏过程、不破坏沉浸感的前提下为玩家提供支持，除非某些情况下确实有必要打断。用户界面应该与游戏相辅相成，并适应不同场景的需求。”他还指出，将手机设计为玩家可以直接拿在手中操作，是整个界面系统的一项重大调整。这种设计能够让玩家更好地代入杰森或露西亚的角色，也有助于让玩家始终沉浸在游戏世界中。为了让这些手机应用以及整体用户体验和用户界面的品质达到游戏本身的制作水准，Rockstar 不断提高标准、重新审视既有设计、探索新的可能性，并通过严格测试和反复迭代完善产品。

articles.title: 美国电玩零售商 GameStop CEO 批评游戏纯数字化：损害玩家和零售商利益
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，据游戏媒体 IGN 今天报道，美国电玩零售商 GameStop CEO 瑞安 · 科恩近期公开批评游戏业界转向纯数字化，称这种趋势不仅对玩家不利，也对公司业务产生不利影响。科恩表示：“消费者购买游戏后应该能够自行出售、以旧换新，或者把游戏借给朋友。毫无疑问，全面转向数字化发行损害了玩家利益，也导致 GameStop 受损。”虽然这名 CEO 没有指名道姓地批评厂商，但《GTA 6》不推出实体光盘版的决定，似乎并未影响这款游戏的整体商业表现。分析师估计，本作正式发售前的预购量已接近 2000 万份。科恩突然为实体光盘发声多少有些讽刺。据IT之家此前援引彭博社消息，他几个月前还称索尼停产实体游戏盘对 GameStop 来说无关紧要，公司营收大头已转向收藏品领域。

articles.title: 尘封 21 年的宝马 E65 世代 L7 概念车重见天日：5.5 米车身，全球仅此一台
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，宝马手里似乎总有没公开过的 7 系。据外媒 motor1 今天（19 日）晚间报道，宝马经典车部门又翻出一段品牌往事，展示了一辆尘封 21 年、仅造过一台的 L7 概念车。这回的原型是 E65 一代 7 系。宝马拿来一辆克里斯 · 班戈时代经过中期改款的 2005 年款 760Li，把车身拉长约 51 厘米，进一步提高了豪华程度，也为后排乘客腾出了宽敞得多的空间。IT之家附上视频如下：报道认为，这辆深蓝色的 L7 概念车，或是宝马当年拿来回应迈巴赫的作品。彼时，迈巴赫仍是独立品牌，旗下拥有 57、62 两款长度不同的超豪华车型。宝马把加长的位置选在 B 柱，与上一代 E38 L7 的做法一样。加长后，后门明显变长，多出来的空间全留给了后排乘客。E65 L7 全长约 5.53 米，比作为原型的长轴版 760Li 长约 35 厘米，比现款 7 系长约 14 厘米，和标准轴距版劳斯莱斯古思特差不多长。前后门之间拉长了一截，让本就气势十足的 E65 更显厚重。单凭车身比例，宝马就让这辆加长轿车有了辨识度，无须再用夸张的造型抢眼。宝马把后排做成了一间私人休息室。车内铺着奶油色真皮，配有木饰板，后排乘客还有一块专用天窗。中控台里还藏着冰箱，旁边另有能竖着放瓶子的储物格。坐在后排，双腿几乎能完全伸直。宝马早在 E65 概念车之前就做过更豪华的 7 系。1997 年至 2001 年，宝马以搭载 5.4L V12 发动机的 750iL 为基础，共造了 899 辆 E38 L7，比普通长轴版 7 系还要长约 25 厘米。时间来到今天，宝马准备再次把 7 系推向更高端的市场。2027 年，新成立的宝马 ALPINA 品牌将推出一款更豪华的 7 系，定位介于常规旗舰车型和劳斯莱斯之间。

articles.title: Uber 前 CEO 卡兰尼克声援黄仁勋：若英伟达员工罢工要求其复职，愿亲自参与
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 19 日消息，Uber 前首席执行官特拉维斯 · 卡兰尼克（Travis Kalanick）表示，如果英伟达员工发起集体罢工，要求黄仁勋复职，他愿意站出来支持，甚至亲自参与行动。卡兰尼克表示：“我会带着一个镶满晶圆的扩音器，前往英伟达总部，身边还会有大批希望参与罢工的英伟达员工，以及众多企业首席执行官和创始人。”这里提到的晶圆，是制造 AI 芯片所使用的基础材料。当地时间周三，卡兰尼克在奥斯汀举行的 TomorrowX 峰会上发表了上述言论。这位 Uber 前 CEO 透露，他曾向黄仁勋发送过截图，内容是 2017 年有关 Uber 员工发起请愿、要求他复职的新闻报道。当年，Uber 一名前工程师指控公司存在性骚扰及人力资源管理问题，由此引发对企业职场文化的调查。在舆论和各方压力下，卡兰尼克最终辞去 Uber CEO 一职。卡兰尼克在 TomorrowX 峰会上回忆称，自己当时给黄仁勋发消息时写道：“请愿不错，但集体罢工更有力。”不过，黄仁勋并没有回复这条消息。在峰会现场，卡兰尼克还穿上了一件黑色皮夹克，模仿黄仁勋标志性的穿衣风格。与他一同登台的还有安东尼奥 · 格拉西亚斯（Antonio Gracias），后者是埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）的长期盟友和投资人。格拉西亚斯看到卡兰尼克的穿着后打趣道：“你这件衣服看起来很像黄仁勋的。”卡兰尼克回应称：“没错，我们得让黄仁勋回来。”IT之家注意到，谈及人工智能的未来，卡兰尼克表示，AI 应该按照人类的意愿发展，而不是凌驾于人类之上，成为所谓的“AI 霸主”。他补充说：“黄仁勋是最有可能为我们争取这种自由的人，他一直以来也在为此努力。”卡兰尼克认为，现场所有人都应该支持黄仁勋复职，因为仅仅是维护这一原则，就足以成为支持他的理由。他还强调：“大家也应该关注正义和正当程序。”尽管黄仁勋周二表示，如果有机会复职，他将感到“荣幸”，而且要求其复职的网络请愿签名人数已经超过 20 万，但英伟达董事会目前并未考虑让他重新担任 CEO。对于推动黄仁勋复职一事，卡兰尼克最后表示：“让我们为正确的事情而战，尽最大努力争取。我们无法决定最终结果，但至少要全力以赴。”

articles.title: Google 杀入 Jev 核心赛道：Gemini Decision 1 五项基准领先两项落后
articles.content: Jev 拿下的 75 亿美元估值曾被质疑是一场泡沫。现在 Google 用一款多模态决策模型告诉市场：这不是泡沫，是赛道。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑  峰                                                                                                       谷歌正式入场了。刚刚，谷歌发布 Gemini Decision 1，正式向 两个月前引爆决策模型品类的 TypeSafe Jev发起挑战。和 Jev 一样，这款模型不生成任何文本，只计算供程序直接驱动 Agent 执行的候选项概率和置信度，不需要逐 Token 生成答案，连输出 Token 费用也省了。更大的突破出现在并行计算上。Gemini Decision 1 可以在同一份上下文中处理至多 1000 项独立判断，而且支持文本、图像、音频、视频和 PDF 混合输入。对于需要反复检查文档、选择工具、评估任务状态的 Agent，大量原本分散在不同模型调用中的判断，现在可以集中在一轮请求中完成。在数据上，7 项双方均有报告的共享基准中，Gemini Decision 1 赢下 5 项，Jev 在 When2Call 工具调用和 Mind2Web 多模态上仍保持优势（82.0% vs 79.9%，86.8% vs 86.2%）。不过，Gemini 每 100 万输入 Token 收费 0.10 美元，是 Jev 的约 2.38 倍。性能上去了，价格也更贵了，谷歌显然想用更强的多模态能力和批量决策能力打开市场。Jev 在 9 月发布后数周内拿下 75 亿美元估值，a16z 领投 8.7 亿美元，约三分之一财富 500 强被列为客户。但质疑从未消散：厂商自报的“快 193 倍、便宜 445 倍”缺乏第三方复现，原创性争议尚未定论，独立评测指向同一个结论：快和便宜是真的，质量是另一回事。雷峰网Google 此时入场，至少证明了一件事：决策模型不是一场闹剧，而是一个值得巨头押注的品类。01模型怎样跳过文本生成完成决策普通 LLM 处理“从四个工具里选一个”这类任务时，仍然走自回归解码：逐 Token 生成工具名或 JSON，程序再解析执行。模型承担的是开放式文本生成，业务需要的却是有限候选项中的概率判断。Gemini Decision 1 把输出目标改成了候选项评分。开发者提前定义问题、候选集合和判断标准，模型读取输入后，直接返回各候选项的概率分布。整个过程通过单次前向计算完成，不需要逐 Token 生成答案，也没有输出 Token 费用。这和普通的 Structured Output 有明显区别。Structured Output 仍然让模型生成文本，只是通过 Schema 限定 JSON 的字段和格式，Gemini Decision 1 则直接围绕有限候选空间完成评分，返回结果本身就是程序可以读取的数据。这里有一个容易被忽略的细节：不同判断类型返回的概率含义并不相同。Noul 处理二元判断，返回某个条件成立的概率，范围为 0.01—0.99。如果问题本身存在歧义，开发者还可以分别定义什么情况算 Yes、什么情况算 No，减少判断标准不清晰带来的偏差。Choice 处理多分类问题，支持 2—255 个候选项，返回胜出选项以及各候选项的归一化概率，所有候选项概率之和为 1。它适合工具路由、模型选择和任务分类。不过，这种概率分配始终发生在给定的候选集合内，即使所有选项都不符合输入，模型仍会选出一个相对匹配的结果。因此，开发者需要提供 Other 选项，或者额外设置范围检查。Score 的设计更有意思。它并不简单返回一个等级，而是先给有序评分标准中的每个等级分配概率，再计算加权评分。例如，将问题分为 0 级、1 级和 2 级，模型可能给出 0.1、0.7 和 0.2 的概率，最终评分可以落在 1 和 2 之间。这实际上把离散分类扩展成了连续评分，方便程序进行排序和阈值筛选。不过，加权结果会压缩概率分布中的信息：两个输入即使

articles.title: 诺亦腾机器人入选 The Information 2026 全球最具潜力50家初创企业榜单
articles.content: 核心要点（Key Facts）· 在 The Information 于 11 月 11 日发布的“2026 全球最具潜力 50 家初创企业”榜单中，诺亦腾机器人（Noitom Robotics）位列亚洲分区第一。· 根据榜单披露，诺亦腾机器人目前估值已超 5 亿美元，累计股权融资逾 5000 万美元，年营收突破 1000 万美元。· 诺亦腾机器人致力于生产供机器人学习的人类数据。公司在中国深圳和美国加州山景城设有数据工厂，并已与物理 AI（Physical AI）领域的近百家企业展开合作。新加坡，2026年11月18日 —— 全球知名科技商业媒体 The Information 近日正式发布"The 50 Most Promising Startups 2026"榜单（全球最具潜力50家初创企业）。物理 AI 数据公司诺亦腾机器人（Noitom Robotics）在亚洲顶尖初创企业榜单（Top Asia Startups）中名列第一。Fig 1. The Information 2026 全球最具潜力50家初创企业榜单榜单数据显示，诺亦腾机器人当前估值已超5亿美元，股权融资总额超5000万美元，营收超1000万美元。The Information 创办于2013年，重点覆盖科技、人工智能与金融，面向全球60多个国家的商业领袖与专业读者提供原创独家报道和深度分析。The Information 50 榜单旨在发掘各细分赛道中最具龙头潜力的早期初创企业，围绕营收规模、商业模式及增长前景进行严格评估，相关财务数据由记者直接向创始人和投资人采集。诺亦腾机器人创始人兼CEO戴若犁博士表示："The Information 依据营收和增长表现对初创企业进行排名。去年，机器人研发团队对人类动作数据的需求还在千小时量级；今年，这一需求已跃升至数十万小时。同时对这些团队而言，另一个至关重要的问题是：具身模型能否真正从这些数据中学到东西。我们很高兴诺亦腾机器人能够获得 The Information 的认可。此次入选，也印证了解决'数据规模'与'数据可学习性'这两大痛点的巨大商业价值。"不造机器人，专注生产机器人学习的"数据"诺亦腾机器人并不制造机器人。公司专注于生产驱动机器人进化的高质量训练数据——通过自建数据工厂与广泛的线下合作场景，系统化采集人类动作、物体交互及日常行为数据，并通过旗下数据平台 ModalityNet（modalitynet.com），向全球机器人本体厂商与 AI 开发者提供标准化的多模态数据集。2025年正式分拆成立后，诺亦腾机器人凭借团队长达13年的动作捕捉技术积淀，快速构建起全球化的数据产能与服务网络。目前公司规模已超百人，在深圳和美国加州山景城（Mountain View）设有数据工厂，在台北和吉隆坡设有数据采集中心，正积极向全球其他地区拓展。截至目前，公司已与物理 AI 领域近百家企业及研发机构达成深度合作。过去一年融资、产品及研发里程碑不断此次入围 The Information 50，源于过去一年间公司在融资、产品及研发领域接连达成的一系列里程碑成果：2025年11月 — 公司完成由阿尔法公社领投，经纬创投（MPCi）、英诺天使基金等机构跟投的 Pre-A 轮融资。2025年12月 — 公司完成由启明创投领投，阿尔法公社、经纬创投、五源资本等跟投的 Pre-A+ 轮融资。2026年6月 — 诺亦腾机器人正式发布数据平台 ModalityNet，三大旗舰数据集产品同步上线。同期宣布完成数亿元人民币 Pre-A++ 轮融资，获北京市人工智能产业投资基金（顺禧管理）、上海人工智能产业系列基金、深创投等多家头部产业资本，以及阿尔法公社、君联资本、五源资本、经纬创投等老股东超额认购。2026年8月 — 高精度人机交互数据集 HiPHI（High Precision Human Interaction）上线，面向学术科研社区开放。HiPHI 是 HiPHI-MOV（Motion with Object and Vision，含物体与视觉的运动数据）语料库的开放研究子集，依据 ModalityNet 开放研究许可证（MORL v1.0）免费供研究使用，完整 HiPHI-MOV 语料库通过 ModalityNet 进行商业授权。目前在 Hugging Face 及公司分发渠道下载量已突破15,000次。2026年11月 — 在奥斯汀举办的机器人学习大会（CoRL 2026）上，诺亦腾机器人团队三篇论文获主会收录，同期重磅推出全新类别的真实场景人类数据集 ITW-Ego Plus，并公开了 HiPHI 系列的第二个开放研究数据集 HiPHI-Hand，该数据集已被用于

articles.title: 黄仁勋「每天都在用」的 Perplexity 开始重构 Attention，把「判断」做成了一个独立模型
articles.content: Decider v1.3：63 项分类任务准确率达 91.6%，对标 Jev 成本直降 61%。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       刚刚，黄仁勋每天都在用的「AI 导师」 Perplexity 有了新动作：正式推出 Decider v1.3，直接把 AI 系统里的判断能力单独做成了一套模型。Perplexity 这次直接改了模型处理判断任务的方式：同一份上下文可以同时交给多个问题使用，模型只需进行一次前向传播，就能输出各个问题的答案概率。 过去需要反复调用 LLM、生成文本、解析结果的流程，现在可以收敛到一次模型计算中。为了让多个问题共享计算时不互相干扰，Perplexity 还重新设计了 Attention 机制，让共享状态读取全部问题，同时限制问题之间直接交换信息。v1.3 进一步加入 Locate 能力，可以根据字段描述直接定位原文跨度，将判断与文本抽取整合进同一套架构。这套模型已经进入 Perplexity 的生产系统。在一次内部安全审查中，它单日处理了 7000 个 Agent 会话，累计读取 10 亿 token，并推动 14 项规则修复。从技术架构来看，Decider 有三个紧密关联的设计层次：输入端如何把共享上下文与独立问题组织在一起，注意力层如何控制不同问题的信息交互，训练与输出层又如何让同一套模型兼顾分类判断和文本定位。其中，隔离式问题注意力改变了多任务共享计算的底层方式，也是理解整个 Decider 架构的关键切口。01一份上下文，承载多个判断任务Decider 的输入其实是由共享状态（State）和若干问题块（Question）组成。State 保存网页、文档或 Agent 执行记录，Question 描述具体判断目标，并列出候选答案。每个候选项映射到预定义标签 Token，例如 A、B、C，特殊的 <|marker|> Token 则标记答案读取位置。模型处理时，会提取 Marker 对应位置的隐藏状态，交给决策头计算各候选项的分数，再转换为概率分布。这里的决策头由基础模型原有的语言模型输出层改造而来：Perplexity 保留 A、B、C 等候选标签对应的权重行，移除其余词表输出权重，再针对决策任务进行训练。原本用于计算下一个 Token 概率的输出层，由此转为专门处理选项判断。这个设计让任务定义与输出计算分离。调用方可以通过自然语言描述问题，通过选项限定答案空间，模型则负责根据上下文计算各选项的概率。情感分析、自然语言推理、意图检测、实体匹配、内容审核、事实核查和评分，可以采用同一套输入协议，不需要为每种任务单独建立一套模型结构。Perplexity 将数百个公开数据集转换为 State、Question、选项和目标组成的统一训练格式。训练目标既可以是正确标签，也可以是完整的答案概率分布。对于同一段长文本需要执行多项判断的情况，多个 Question 可以放进同一次前向传播，模型只需处理一份共享上下文。不过计算收益需要准确理解：增加问题仍然会增加 Question Token 和注意力计算，Decider 节省的主要是长文本被重复编码的开销，以及生成式模型逐 Token 解码和外部解析的成本。问题数量越多、共享文本越长，复用价值越明显。输出概率还保留了业务策略的调整空间。模型负责给出候选项的概率分布，应用根据误报、漏报的业务代价设置阈值。网页过滤和 Agent 执行审查可以使用不同门槛，无需为每种业务重新训练决策模型。02多任务如何共享信息，互不干扰输入协议确定后，新的问题落在模型内部：多个 Question 同时进入 Transformer，它们之间应该建立怎样的信息连接？Decider 以生成式 LLM 为骨干，原有因果注意力按照文本顺序组织信息，当前位置只能读取自身及前面的 Token。这种结构适合逐

articles.content: 同时拥有理工科训练、结构生物学功底，和系统商科思维的创业者，在AI4S领域里并不常见。    作者丨周蕾    编辑丨岑峰                                                                                                       【编者按】AI4S有时给人“雷声大雨点小”之感，是因为不少人把AI当成了目的本身，拿着锤子满世界找钉子，对科研周期与商业回报的错配却无知无觉。“AI4S青年志”第二篇，我们关注一个可能破解AI4S落地困局的样本。一篇论文，通常只需要2-4位审稿人。但当《Nature Biotechnology》的编辑们打开一篇来自加州大学伯克利分校的投稿时，他们很快意识到，2-4位远远不够。为了覆盖这篇论文涉及的每一个学科，编辑们前后邀请的审稿人数量已经来到了两位数。论文横跨四个领域：合成生物学、材料科学、计算化学，以及技术经济学与碳排放核算。审稿人们上来就说：他们只能看懂属于自己的那一部分，无法对其他部分做出评价。学术论文通常像一辆概念车，但这篇论文，却被以量产车的标准来严苛审视。例如论文已经在实验室里证明，生物反应器中，新型塑料单体的滴度达到了1.84克每升——这是一个符合学术发表标准的数字。但一位材料学背景的审稿人直接追问：“如果这个平台要走向产业化，至少要让我看到几十克每升的可能性。”这些质疑，同时关乎科学和商业。而回应它的人，需要同时听懂四种语言。最终，四个不同领域的专家全部认可了这篇论文，编辑也点了头，论文在今年夏天成功刊发。这篇论文的署名栏里，第一作者只有一个名字：王子龙。在AI for Science的创业浪潮里，跨学科背景并不稀奇。计算机出身的人去学材料，化学出身的人去写代码，这样的故事比比皆是。但像王子龙这样，同时拥有扎实的理工科训练、结构生物学的底层功底，以及从本科阶段就开始的系统商科思维，并且能把这一切翻译成彼此能听懂的语言——这种人在AI4S创业者中，并不常见。借着论文刊发的机会，雷峰网AI科技评论和王子龙完成了一次两个多小时的越洋连线，从中山大学逸仙班的经济学课堂聊到Jay Keasling的实验室，从主动拒绝创业风口聊到放弃教职、投身产业，试图还原这位AI4S青年科学家，在他过去二十年里的每一次关键选择。01像“爱迪生”的底色王子龙儿时的梦想，是成为爱迪生那样的科学家。长大后他意识到，原来爱迪生不光是科学家，同时也是一名商人，而他恰好也将自己培养出了科学家+企业家的双重能力结构。这种能力结构的雏形，最早要追溯到本科时期。王子龙所就读的中大逸仙班，准入门槛极高，采用多学科混合培养的方式，除了数物化生的理工科内容，还有专门开设的经济学课程，由岭南学院的教授整套授课。加之出生于经商家庭，从事零售和分销，王子龙对商业实践已有着十几年的认知。逸仙班的课业负担不轻，但当时的多学科培养，尤其是经济学方面的训练，直到今天仍然在为他的商业工作带来极大的帮助。一方面经济学带给他反直觉的思维和理论，帮助他避免踩坑；另一方面，这套训练也为一位纯科学家在做商业谈判、市场判断时，提供了底气。“基本的商业逻辑、经济逻辑我们都清楚，对外融资、谈合作的时候，精神面貌是不一样的。”2011年，中山大学首次参加MIT创办的iGEM（国际基因工程机器大赛），正在读大三、准备出国留学的王子龙，正是当时参赛的领队和对外主讲人。队伍最终闯入了全球决赛。在MIT的讲台上，他要用英语向评委解释团队的成果；回到实验室，他又得和队友一起解决具体的科学问题。这个比赛最终帮他敲开了合成生物学认知的大门。也是在这个时期，他读到了一篇经典论文：用大肠杆菌和酵母菌全合成青蒿素前体。屠呦呦当年发现的青蒿素，在合成生物学的方法下，得以实现低成本、大规模的生产。而这位论文的作者Jay Keasling，后来成为了他在伯克利的导师。“我们可以改造自然界的微生物，让它们为人类所用，实现不同的功能。”合成生物学最底层的定义，是让每个基因的设计模块化，“像拼乐高一样拼基因，拼出不同的形态和功能。”王子龙被合成生物学深深

articles.title: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. articles.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21827v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene-change split, the background stops helping and starts hurting. Accuracy is 22.8% on full chips and 30.8% when only the vehicle is shown. A SAR foundation model, SARATR-X, leans on the background more than ConvNeXt does (+4 to +6 points with the vehicle removed, in every seed) and does not solve the scene change. articles.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the best frontier models outperform human auditors (Fable 5.1: AUROC 0.73, 32% full identification) within noise and weaker models perform comparably. articles.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21885v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A language model is trained once and frozen. Making it better takes another training run, or a prompt, a harness or extra computation at inference that is gone once the task ends. We show a third way: to our knowledge for the first time, a language model rewrites its own weights by its own reasoning and becomes better, with no gradients and no training. We call this self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer. In earlier work, a frontier model edited a much smaller one; here an open 27B model, given its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, diagnoses its own failure and rewrites the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it never saw. It keeps getting better: it tests its edits on practice problems and submits only what works, each edit improving on the last, and over eight consecutive sessions its accuracy only rises. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed proposals, and (3) they utilize features sampled uniformly from across the target layers, omitting important hidden states. articles.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21937v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open radio access networks (O-RAN). articles.title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21946v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change in which chains are still running. We measure both on MATH-500. articles.title: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21948v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The regulation of Artificial Intelligence is susceptible to various forms of capture by industry actors that hold undue influence over the policymaking process, due in part to their information advantage in developing these technologies. In the following paper, we investigate the roles of public commenters in providing evidence to potential regulation in the USA. We build a corpus of 40 potential regulations, and 2,664 public comments submitted by a variety of stakeholders. We computationally process these texts to extract evidence meant to inform regulators, in the form of formal citations and informal references. We find significant differences in the type and amount of evidence supplied: Holding comment length constant, business commenters introduce altogether less evidence, and government, university, and civil society commenters provide significantly more research and legal sources. articles.title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21950v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 ProteinGym baselines. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21978v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and budgets, while hosts distribute the public program and may retain private services server-side. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. We specify the design: storage record, budget-derived retention, append-only read path, and bounded aggregation. articles.title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change. arXiv:2611.22030v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An agent resource's value depends on its backbone and companion resources and is known only after execution. Token-based generators remain tied to their training catalog, while independent resource scoring misses complementarities and reused bundles target other tasks. A fine-tuned generator reads resource descriptions and recombines candidates through constrained beam search, allowing new resources without retraining. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22033v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. articles.title: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22043v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood search, Lagrangian bounds and reduced-cost fixing. articles.title: MedGuardBench: A Patient-Oriented Benchmark for Personalized Guardrail Development
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22069v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Safety is personal: the same action can be safe for one person but unsafe for another. Yet current guardrails judge content without considering who is affected. Using medication safety, we introduce \textit{patient-conditioned medication guarding}, which predicts a safety verdict and 17 risk categories from a patient profile and prescription. Abstract: An expert who corrects a concept prediction, such as a BI-RADS descriptor in breast ultrasound, expects the diagnosis to improve. Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer theoretical energy-efficiency advantages over conventional deep networks, but realizing these advantages on vision tasks requires sparse spike representations that naive rate-coding methods fail to provide. We combine biologically motivated spike-encoding schemes with two training improvements: Rouser adaptive-threshold surrogate gradients and Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (K-FAC) second-order optimization. The spike encoding schemes experimented with are rate coding, latency coding, DVS-style delta modulation, and Difference-of-Gaussians (DoG) filtering. Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST demonstrate that biologically inspired encoders yield the largest accuracy gains in capacity-constrained regimes and serve as an effective parameter-efficiency lever. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23246v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nearly all current methods for computing reachable sets of nonlinear dynamics propagate them with truncated Taylor expansions plus rigorous remainders. The expansion is pointwise: once its argument is a whole set rather than a point, one polynomial must stay accurate across that set, and it reaches only as far as its disc of convergence. The limit binds hardest on the rational terms and sigmoid gates of modern controllers: smooth as these look on the real line, in the complex plane they blow up at points just off the real axis, closer as a gate sharpens, and those points cap the set width a Taylor expansion can cover, most tightly on the switching surface where the controller decides. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23247v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A binary probability estimate may be used by several decision makers with different error costs. Proper scoring rules can emphasize selected probability thresholds, but a single average threshold distribution need not give a good worst-case regret guarantee. We study the choice of a proper loss when the threshold distribution belongs to a finite specified family. Among integrable loss weights with a positive pointwise floor and a fixed total mass, we derive the weight that minimizes the sharp, distribution-free multiplier from surrogate regret to threshold-averaged decision regret. The solution clips a rescaled upper envelope of the threshold densities at the prescribed floor; its normalization is found by a one-dimensional root search. We give proofs of sharpness, optimality, and stability under density misspecification, as well as a limitation for atomic threshold laws. Abstract: In recent years, machine learning (ML) techniques have emerged as promising tools for accurate and timely diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) which is an incurable neurodegenerative disorder. Abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) inference differs substantially from conventional LLM serving, featuring long input sequences, wide beam search, and only a few fixed output tokens. Abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on not only individual agent behaviors but also the interactions that connect agents, including message exchanges and task dependencies. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23388v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. Fortunately, an LLM agent can take over this design by refining the recipe over rounds of building and evaluating candidates, so that more rounds lead to better recipes. However, evaluating one quantized reasoning model takes tens of GPU-hours, and combining methods from different codebases means porting each to the new architecture by hand. We present QDA, a system in which an agent designs the recipe for each model and precision. Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model to match a teacher model based on its own generations. When using OPD, one must choose whether to apply it at the sequence or token level and which divergence to minimize. However, despite the wide adoption of OPD in practice, the formal understanding of which OPD objective is appropriate for a given setting is limited. Toward addressing this gap, we theoretically analyze how the choice of OPD objective governs which tokens are prioritized, in what order, and how efficiently. Our analysis reveals that sequence-level OPD exhibits a future agreement bias, which myopic token-level objectives avoid. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23427v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Plasticity and stability in continual learning are typically studied at the entire-model level and in a task-agnostic manner, yet prior work has reported divergent conclusions across settings. In a controlled synthetic environment with clean measurement, we show a double dissociation: query-key (QK) and value-output (VO) projections are the most plastic on procedural tasks, whereas MLPs are the most plastic on declarative memorization. Stability, however, does not simply mirror plasticity: when learning a new procedure, updating QK retains over half of the stored declarative memory, while updating MLPs retains far less and updating VO loses roughly four-fifths. articles.title: Sleep2Word: Peripheral-to-EEG Translation via Duration-Aware Wordization
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Estimating full-night electroencephalography (EEG) spectrograms from peripheral measurements could extend EEG-informed sleep analysis to recordings acquired without EEG. This task requires compact representations of signals with different temporal structures. We introduce Sleep2Word, a framework for translating respiration, electrocardiography (ECG), or photoplethysmography (PPG) into EEG spectrograms through duration-aware physiological words. Building on context-dependent chunking, Sleep2Word groups physiological embeddings into variable-duration chunks and jointly quantizes their content and duration into modality-specific wordbooks. A block-autoregressive translator then predicts target EEG word identities and occurrence-specific duration refinements within fixed-duration blocks. articles.title: MInfoVisQA: A Multilingual Benchmark for Information-Rich Visual Question Answering
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21644v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel in vision-language tasks; yet, whether they maintain consistent understanding of information-rich visuals (InfoVis) when the surface language changes remains unclear. To quantify this capability, we introduce MInfoVisQA, a parallel benchmark with 8,960 QA configurations derived from 128 seed instances across 24 languages. We construct seed-matched, language-parallel visuals and QA pairs by disentangling numerical-structural data from text and programmatically synchronizing translated labels. We evaluate 25 MLLMs under two settings: Language-Aligned QA (LQA, matching visual-text languages) and Cross-Language QA (XQA, fixed QA language with varying visual languages). The results show that aggregate accuracy masks substantial robustness gaps: two models with comparable mean LQA accuracy (80.4\%) exhibit performance spreads of 7.8 and 20.3 percentage points across languages. articles.title: Limite 1B - Violetto: Technical Report
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Limite 1B - Violetto, a one-billion-parameter model designed for high-throughput mathematical reasoning. Limite is trained from scratch on 237 billion tokens from a carefully curated, mathematics-centric corpus and supports context lengths of up to 131k tokens. Its architecture and training recipe were developed together to maximize reasoning capability while keeping training and inference costs low. Post-training combines knowledge distillation, targeted supervised fine-tuning, and RLVR on a curated curriculum. Limite achieves 94.01% on AIME 2026 and 74.25% on BeyondAIME, placing it among models many times its size on our evaluation suite. The model is deliberately only lightly instruction-tuned: it is intended primarily as a single-turn mathematical solver and as a fast, parallel component of larger systems, rather than as a general-purpose assistant. articles.title: FieldGuide: A Corpus Map for Token-Efficient Agentic Document Exploration
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21647v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative AI agents can help journalists explore large document collections. But exploratory workflows can require substantial token use and time, especially when the task is broad and the relevant subquestions are not yet known. This paper introduces FieldGuide, an agent-facing corpus map that organizes a document collection into a topic hierarchy and exposes tools for corpus orientation, scoped search, and bounded reading. I evaluate FieldGuide on five journalistic document-exploration tasks using 38 Chicago Police Department public-records documents, comparing it with raw-file access and retrieval-augmented generation. Across the five tasks, FieldGuide used 27% fewer tokens and 41% less elapsed time than raw-file access; relative to RAG, it used 38% fewer tokens and 21% less elapsed time. articles.title: Can an LLM dream? Testing the overfitted brain hypothesis on an agent with text memory
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21648v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hoel (2021) proposed that dreams distort replayed experience so that the brain does not overfit to recent events. We test this hypothesis on an LLM agent (Claude Opus 5.5) that stores what it learns in a text memory and rewrites that memory each night from the day's conversation transcript. The agent goes through ten simulated days of conversation built from LongMemEval. We corrupt 5, 10, 20 or 40 percent of the transcript's turns before each nightly rewrite in one of two ways. Detail corruption changes one or two details in a turn to plausible wrong ones, or replaces the turn with one by the same speaker from an earlier day. Random-text corruption replaces half of the selected turns with a passage of Moby-Dick and inserts Moby-Dick words into the other half. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21649v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we propose an alternative approach to human evaluation of literary fictions by employing LLMs themselves as evaluators within the GrAImes framework. We apply this methodology to assess human-written and AI-generated microfictions in Spanish, to five PhD professors in literature and sixteen literary enthusiasts, and to short stories in both Spanish and English. By comparing the evaluations performed by LLMs with those of human judges, we examine the degree of alignment and divergence between both perspectives, thereby assessing the feasibility of LLMs as auxiliary literary evaluators. Our analysis focuses on the alignment of responses from LLMs with those of human evaluators, providing insights into the potential of LLMs in literary assessment. articles.title: From Preference Data to Personalization: Tracing Sycophancy in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21650v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sycophancy in large language models is often measured as agreement with the user, yet agreement can be appropriate when the user's claim is valid, their preference is genuine, or their experience warrants acknowledgment. We study sycophancy as inappropriate agreement: validating a claim, preference, or self-assessment when the context calls for correction, qualification, or resistance. We introduce a validity-aware sycophancy grader and SycoDrift, a persona-targeted evaluation set of 3,298 validity-annotated probes with controlled annotations for user openness and stakes. We use this framework to analyze three sources of agreement pressure: human preference data, automated judge specification, and in-context personalization. First, preference for validating responses in human datasets (Chatbot Arena, HH-RLHF, Community Alignment) is weak and concentrated where agreement is often appropriate. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21651v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A controller that resamples an answer, escalates to a larger model, or abstains is usually justified by a confidence signal. Three claims about such a signal do not follow from one another: it ranks answers (discrimination), it supports withholding some of them (selective prediction), and it changes an answer for the better (correction utility). We give an exact decomposition of the third into gated recoveries minus gated harms, which bounds whether a comparison can succeed before it is run: a gate that only replaces a proposal can act only where the base policy was already wrong, so the initial error count caps the discordant pairs any correct gate can produce. When that cap falls below the count a paired test needs, the experiment cannot return a positive result for a working mechanism, nor distinguish one from a gate that never fired. articles.title: Evaluating Semantic Insensitivity in Financial Sentiment Analysis: Implications for Sustainable Financial Decision-Making
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21653v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Financial sentiment analysis is critical for automated trading, portfolio management, and risk assessment, heavily relying on models like FinBERT. Despite high benchmark accuracy, these models remain vulnerable to subtle adversarial text modifications, threatening the integrity of algorithmic decision-making. In this paper, we propose Agent-driven Semantic Inversion (ASI), a novel adversarial attack framework targeting financial sentiment models through domain-specific semantic manipulation. Utilizing an LLM-powered multi-agent pipeline, our approach identifies eligible financial news sentences and applies targeted lexical substitutions. We empirically evaluate ASI against FinBERT, one of the most widely deployed financial sentiment models. articles.title: Token Commitment as a Control Surface for Steering Masked Diffusion Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21669v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Masked diffusion models repeatedly predict provisional tokens before a sampler decides which predictions become permanent. Existing inference-time steering methods primarily modify activations, logits, or denoising trajectories, while treating this commitment policy as a fixed decoding detail. We instead study token commitment as a diffusion-specific control surface and separate it into two decisions: which tokens to commit and how many tokens to commit at each step. For the first, we introduce counterfactual target-aware commitment, which ranks unresolved positions by a mixture of model confidence and leave-one-token-out target contribution. For the second, we introduce calibrated adaptive budgets driven by target progress and confidence. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21804v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision-making contexts, where interactions among components can introduce fairness risks that remain undetected when auditing components or collective outcomes in isolation. As LLM-based multi-agent systems become more prevalent, understanding how biased information propagates through agent interactions is essential for assessing their fairness. We introduce a controlled bias injection framework that replaces selected agent responses with predefined biased ones, enabling an intervention-based analysis of how network topology and injection configurations shape system behavior. We propose decision divergence metrics that quantify the effects of these interventions at the agent, network, and system levels, and evaluate five topologies on three binary classification tasks using LLMs from the Qwen and Gemma families. articles.title: SimAI: Mechanistic User Simulation through Psychological Network Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21808v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Realistic user simulation enables the study of human interactions when direct experimentation is costly or potentially harmful. However, existing simulators largely overlook the psychological mechanisms that drive user behavior. We introduce SimAI, a framework for mechanistic user simulation that models how psychological factors interact to shape user responses. To overcome the challenge of supervising open-ended behavior, we propose a graph reconstruction objective that provides graph-level rewards based on how well simulated conversations reflect the underlying psychological relationships. To support this approach, we construct PSYCHE, a dataset of 18,576 profile-network pairs derived from 516 psychotherapy cases. Automatic evaluations show that SimAI achieves greater simulation and behavioral diversity than existing patient simulators while maintaining strong profile alignment. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21823v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in Persian law remains challenging because benchmarks lack realism, grounding, and coverage of legal reasoning. Existing resources are either synthetically generated from statutory texts, lacking natural information needs, or derived from informal legal question--answer sources without explicit linkage to authoritative legal documents, making them unsuitable for rigorous evaluation of grounded legal reasoning. To address this gap, we introduce TUSI-Bench, a structured Persian legal benchmark designed for the evaluation of RAG-based systems. TUSI-Bench is built upon a multi-layered legal knowledge framework containing 7,261 legal articles and integrating codified statutes, legal commentaries, doctrinal writings, and Supreme Court unification rulings. articles.title: Knowing Which, Not How Much: Language Models Order Party Positions They Cannot Place
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21878v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models are increasingly asked where real actors stand: what a party's platform prioritises, what an institution has committed to. Such judgments are gradable, carrying both an order and a magnitude. Nearly every benchmark that tests them asks about one entity at a time, then reads that score as the model's knowledge of the domain. Order and magnitude, however, need not be acquired together. Text about social entities carries far more comparison than measurement, so a model may hold a dependable ordering with no anchored scale beneath it. We ask whether a model can place a documented social position on a scale or only order the actors it compares, and what that means for how such knowledge is measured. We test this on party positions in Japan and South Korea, where the Comparative Manifesto Project's coded data supplies a rare external answer key. articles.title: Call-Efficient ICD-10 Code Prediction via Supervised Candidate Generation and Selective LLM Invocation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.21891v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic assignment of ICD-10 codes from short clinical diagnosis text is a practical medical text classification and normalization task. The task is difficult because diagnosis phrases are short and noisy, the ICD-10 label space is hierarchical, and the class distribution is strongly imbalanced. This paper presents a call-efficient ICD-10 code prediction pipeline that combines transformer embeddings, tree-based supervised candidate generation, candidate-level reranking, and a gated LLM assistance. The evaluation uses a leakage-safe validation protocol: model and threshold selection are based on out-of-fold cross-validation predictions, while final reporting is performed on a locked test set with no shared source-file groups. The supervised conditional parent-code candidate generator reaches 74.32% Top-1 accuracy on the locked test set and 93.05% Top-10 candidate coverage. Abstract: Controlled studies of latent two-hop reasoning train transformers to predict only the answer, whereas language models are trained to predict every token. articles.title: DiagTrace: An Interactive Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.22009v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on medical question answering and diagnostic reasoning benchmarks. However, existing evaluations typically provide all patient information upfront and assess only the final diagnosis or rationale. This setup ignores the need to acquire diagnostic evidence incrementally from incomplete information in real-world diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we introduce DiagTrace, a source-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can reconstruct the documented diagnostic trajectory through interactive information seeking. Each benchmark instance is built from a PubMed Central case report and includes an initial presentation, an event bank, a clinical course, and diagnostic references. DiagTrace contains 510 cases across eight specialties, with 225 used to evaluate four LLMs on clinical-course alignment, interaction quality, and efficiency. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23416v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Streaming 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) allows for online reconstruction of dynamic scenes from multi-view videos for Free Viewpoint Video (FVV). Current time and storage efficient methods rely on selecting a subset of anchor Gaussians and neighborhood interpolation for fast streamable 3DGS. However, these methods can overlook object-specific motion and introduce inconsistencies near object boundaries. We propose OCLDA-GS, an object-centric streaming framework that dynamically reallocates object and motion-aware Gaussian anchors to allocate anchor Gaussian support for objects undergoing large motion while at the same time, restricting the gaussian neighborhood within object groups for more precise object boundaries. Furthermore, it estimates object-wise rigid transformations (e.g. a hand moving) and leverages these estimates to learn per-anchor local deformation correction for small deformations (e.g. wrinkles on a shirt). articles.title: Autoregressive View Model
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23417v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present the Autoregressive View Model (AVM), which generates a scene as a stream of views without constructing an explicit 3D representation. Through a unified in-context interface, AVM conditions on images or videos to generate short clips along a requested camera path. Visual context grounds reconstruction and interpolation, while a learned prior enables extrapolation into unseen regions. AVM retrieves relevant views from inputs and generated history to form a bounded active context. We fine-tune a pretrained bidirectional video diffusion transformer with flow matching in an N-in-1-out formulation. We then tune a causal model on its own rollouts to improve photorealism, reduce denoising steps, and limit long-horizon drift. We scale training to approximately 8M scenes and video clips. articles.title: Bits, Not Boxes: Label-Free Layer Selection for Visual Localization in VLMs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23432v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attention maps cheaply show where a vision-language model (VLM) looks, but attention sinks make them unreliable for localization. Contrasting the question with a generic prompt suppresses sinks, yet only some layers localize the queried object. Existing methods find these layers with box annotations or fixed rules. We show that attention itself can identify them. A question changes how much a head attends to the image and where this attention goes. The two effects separate exactly, and the second, measured in bits on unlabeled questions, indicates which layers localize. WhereBits turns these where-to-look bits into a layer prior and combines it with per-head contrastive scores. Its three design constants were fixed once on labeled COCO data, and a new model or resolution needs only unlabeled questions. articles.title: TransFIRA+: Transfer Learning for Biometric Recognizability Assessment
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23442v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Biometric recognition in surveillance, video, and web imagery must contend with extreme variation in pose, blur, illumination, occlusion, and distance, where visual quality metrics fail to predict whether inputs are recognizable to the deployed encoder. Existing face image quality assessment methods rely on visual heuristics, curated annotations, or costly generative pipelines, leaving their predictions detached from the encoder's decision geometry. We introduce TransFIRA, a lightweight framework that grounds recognizability directly in embedding space. TransFIRA derives class-center similarity (CCS) and class-center angular separation (CCAS) from a pretrained encoder's embeddings and learns to predict them from images without quality annotations. articles.title: NIRJALA: Draining the Sea out of Gaussian Splatting with Three-Path Optics and Reversible Physics
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23450v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Water does not just tint an underwater photograph; it rewrites it. Each pixel mixes attenuated scene radiance, backscattered light, and scene light scattered forward on its way to the camera, and many combinations of scene and water explain the same pixels. Most Gaussian-splatting methods for underwater scenes model only the first two effects and remove the water by dividing by a transmission that decays exponentially with range, so their inversion gain grows without bound. We present NIRJALA (Sanskrit for "without water"), a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that recovers water-free appearance and geometry together. TRIVENI, a three-path image formation model, adds a range-saturating forward-scattering term to direct transmission and backscatter; we prove that this keeps the inversion gain bounded at every range and bound how errors in the estimated backscatter and attenuation propagate into the recovered colours. articles.title: Reference-Guided Data Curation for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pretraining
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23484v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training 3D vision-language models (VLMs) on large medical imaging datasets collected across institutions is constrained by data quality. Vast, uncurated pools of image-report pairs are characterized by redundancy, class imbalance, and cross-institutional heterogeneity. We address this challenge of data curation for improving 3D VLM pretraining by proposing an offline, training-free, reference-guided data curation recipe. Our approach leverages a small, high-quality reference set to independently extract quality signals for each modality of a large, uncurated pool and merges them through a rank-aggregation step into a single ranking that guides sample selection. We validate this method on datasets comprising 35k 3D abdominal CT volume-report pairs from two institutions and 58k 2D chest X-ray image-report pairs. articles.title: GRID-UAV: Geometry and Ray-depth Integrated Decision-making for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23491v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) encode images with 2D encoders that capture little 3D structure. A common approach is to feed the policy estimated depth, but a UAV chooses its own altitude, must judge distances tens of meters away, where monocular depth is less reliable, and must relate its forward and downward views. On long aerial routes, adding depth features directly brings no significant gain (42.5% vs. 42.6% success), so we study how 3D information should be given to the policy. Analyzing flight failures, we find that two forms of 3D grounding fail in opposite ways: explicit 3D lifting of depth collides less on the way but more often fails to finish at the target, while implicit alignment with a 3D geometry model finishes more often but collides more. We propose GRID, which combines both: (1) it lifts monocular depth into ray-corrected 3D positions in the UAV's frame for both cameras, and (2) during training only, it aligns it

articles.title: MedHarness: A Unified Budgeted Runtime for Reliable Medical Imaging Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23501v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical imaging agents already return answers on heterogeneous imaging surfaces, yet deployment still faces a limited verification budget where each wrong accept can harm clinical trust. When a thin check and a deeper evidence pass disagree on the same case, deciding when to stop, open more evidence, repair, or reject without a shared controller remains ill-posed. Tool-using workflows often lock a surface-specific evidence order per dataset, or a private always-open full-depth verification path; those pipelines stay costly, leave many wrong accepts, and cannot share one controller across modalities. We present MedHarness, a registered multi-surface runtime reliability layer that reformulates post-answer control as shared decision-object attachment after a proposer's initial prediction. articles.title: Trust the Ray, Not the Depth: Ray-Lateral Agreement for Multi-View 3D Human Pose Fusion
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23513v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Put a monocular mesh estimator behind every camera of a calibrated rig, and the reconstructed bodies land a meter or more apart. The cause is geometric: each estimate sits at the depth implied by a focal length the network assumed, not the one the camera has. Its error therefore points almost entirely along its own viewing ray, and the calibration tells us that direction exactly. To address this, we introduce the Ray-Lateral Agreement (RLA), which follows one rule: trust the ray, not the depth. RLA first slides every estimate along its own rays, which removes the depth bias and leaves the shape untouched. It then fuses the views one point at a time, under a Gaussian error whose precision follows each viewing ray. The maximum-likelihood solution is closed-form, interpolates between averaging and midpoint triangulation, and stays well conditioned where triangulation is singular. articles.title: Beyond the Sink Token: Sink-Guided Key Editing in Vision-Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23516v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In vision-language models (VLMs), a few sink tokens attract a disproportionate share of attention. While previous studies have examined why these tokens attract attention, we investigate how the sink-key direction affects attention to image and question tokens. Across four probed VLMs, boosting the magnitude of positive sink-aligned components increases attention on average, whereas boosting negative components decreases it; these responses persist through later layers. This identifies the native sink key as a reference for controlling attention beyond its own position. Motivated by this finding, we propose SHRINK, a training-free method that partially reduces sink-aligned components across visible keys during generation. On nine benchmarks under sampled reasoning, it improves mean accuracy by 5.1 and 2.7 percentage points on LLaVA-OneVision-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-3B, with smaller gains on the other two main models, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Gemma-3-

articles.title: ORGANIC3D: Grounding 3D CT Vision Language Models in Organ Level Image Text Coupling
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23529v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in 3D computed tomography (CT) classification, but high accuracy does not reflect whether their predictions rely on the correct anatomical evidence. We introduce ORGANIC3D, a framework for evaluating and improving organ level image text alignment through controlled anatomical interventions. Our benchmark assesses 12 vision encoder checkpoints and 7 generative VLMs using matched patient comparisons, organ erasure, lesion replacement, and laterality perturbations, revealing substantial alignment failures even among top performing models. To learn organ level image text correspondence, ORGANIC3D aligns each finding sentence with the anatomy aware image features and trains on edited scans to anchor this alignment in the organ's image evidence. articles.title: Layer-Matched Sparse Attention for Low-Redundancy 3D Reconstruction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23554v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: VGGT reconstructs cameras and geometry from unposed images in one pass, but its global attention grows quadratically with the number of views. Training-free accelerators thin this attention and work well on redundant video, but lose pose accuracy when views share little geometry. This paper traces these losses to two kinds of cross-view information that a uniform sparse approximation can fail to preserve together: diffuse layers aggregate distributed context, whereas matching layers depend on query-specific interactions that carry little attention mass. A per-layer statistic measures the log-mass missed by a mean token. Its row-free proxy is the logit variance, and it selects the estimator for each layer. Diffuse layers use shared, importance-sampled hub keys, with log-weights that make the softmax numerator and denominator unbiased. articles.title: DOCK: Dual-Stream-Inspired Self-Supervised Object-Centric Representations Grounded in Robot Kinematics
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23578v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Latent-space planners select actions by comparing the embedding of a predicted future image with that of a goal image. This assumes that distance in the embedding reflects how far the scene is from the goal. We profile this assumption with simulator-executed futures, which removes prediction error. For six frozen DINO and V-JEPA encoders, feature distance barely tracks the object's distance to its goal: the rank correlation is at most 0.11, against 0.87 for object-mask centroids. It is dominated by background and robot patches, and frozen-feature readouts capture the arm far better than the object. Inspired by the ventral (what) and dorsal (where/how) visual streams, we propose DOCK, which learns an object representation whose changes agree with measured physical motion. articles.title: ExiST: Existence-Aware Self-Training for Semi-Supervised Multi-Organ Segmentation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23581v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Semi-supervised multi-organ segmentation should learn more than a dozen organs from a handful of labeled scans, and the smallest organs occupy less than one percent of the foreground. We identify a failure mode of self-training that is specific to this regime. When a teacher misses a small organ in a scan, every voxel of that organ receives the confident pseudo-label background, and the student is trained toward the organ absence. Repeated over many scans, this loop extinguishes tail organs. In a pilot study, removing the gallbladder from the pseudo-labels reduced its Dice on AMOS from 36.5 to 1.0. We argue that a missing organ should be treated as unresolved rather than absent and propose Existence-aware Self-Training (ExiST). It builds pseudo-labels by leave-one-out consensus of independently trained networks, screens them with a quality gate on validation scans, and infers, per scan and per organ, whether the organ was found. articles.title: GRAFT: Graph-Regularized Prototype Fields for Realistic Test-Time Adaptation of VLMs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23591v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unlabeled test data can improve the zero-shot classifier of a vision-language model, yet transductive and test-time adaptation methods often fall below the zero-shot baseline when only a few vocabulary classes are present in a batch or when streams are correlated. We trace this failure to a shared design: every class owns independent parameters estimated from its own samples, so absent or rare classes are left at biased text anchors or fitted to foreign samples. We propose Graph-Regularized Anchor-displacement Field Transduction (GRAFT), which models the adapted prototypes as text anchors plus a displacement field that is partially pooled over a semantic class graph through a Gaussian Markov random field prior, together with an explicit class-presence model. articles.title: VIBRA: Backward-Compatible Cross-Modal Retrieval with Consensus Barycenters
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23606v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Backward-compatible retrieval enables a new encoder to query the gallery that an old model has already encoded, so that a cross-modal retrieval system can be upgraded without re-encoding billions of items. Existing compatible methods either fit the old query and stay near the accuracy of the old model, or run the old and the new encoder for every query. We propose VIBRA, which matches relevance on the old gallery, corrects the errors of a single model with the barycenter of several views, which is itself a query in the old space, and trains the new encoder to inherit this consensus, so that models absent at deployment still shape every query. We show that the barycenter gains margin over the average of its views exactly when their hardest irrelevant items differ, and we characterize the share of this gain that one encoder can reach. articles.title: Weight Space Programming for Vision Language Model Repair
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23615v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In weight-space programming, a language model edits a network's weights directly, without gradients. We ask what a successful repair of this kind relies on. We plant faults in the weights of two vision-language models, SmolVLM-256M and LFM2-VL-450M, and check each edit made by a coding agent against the original weights. Without being told where to look, the agent finds rescaled rows in the projector and noise in the vision encoder of both models, infers the unknown scale factors, restores most or all of the rescaled weights to their exact original values, and returns accuracy to near its original level; programs that it writes from such weights repair unseen checkpoints of the same model without feedback. These repairs depend on a trace of how the faults were computed. articles.title: Isthmus: Bridging Supervision Islands Restores Uncertainty and Stability in One-Step Flows
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23616v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: One-step flow maps are increasingly used as posterior samplers, where the point of sampling is the uncertainty that the samples carry. We find that the one-step sampler loses this uncertainty and becomes less stable. Compared with multi-step samples of the same network, its samples lose variance and decorrelate. Supervising the one-step jump directly makes this worse; the samples collapse further toward the conditional mean and break down when training is extended. We trace both failures to the locations where training places its pairs of start and end times. Only pairs on the diagonal of the time triangle receive targets from data, and the pair used for one-step sampling is either left unsupervised or supervised on an island, a set of pairs that the self-consistency identity does not connect to the diagonal, where the objective neither determines the one-step map nor anchors its training. articles.title: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23499v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models predict discrete action tokens with the next-token objective of their vision-language backbone, so the action tokenizer defines the interface between the policy and the robot. In bimanual manipulation, the two arms share a repertoire of movements yet coordinate through complementary roles, and an action representation should capture both. However, most existing tokenizers encode both arms as a single concatenated action vector, in which motion patterns common to the two arms are not shared and cross-arm dependencies remain entangled within each token. The policy must therefore learn both aspects implicitly. articles.title: Learning and Control in Physically Coupled Dynamical Systems
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23502v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce TAG (Testbed for Autonomous Games), a compact, low-cost robotic platform for studying learning and control in physically coupled dynamical systems. TAG combines an actively tilted and steered ball-in-maze board with a top-mounted rotary inverted pendulum. The pendulum's reaction torque and vibration disturb the board and marble, while the board's tilt, driven by the maze-solving policy, simultaneously disturbs the pendulum's balance. The main challenge in learning control policies for each subsystem is accounting for the impact of one subsystem's dynamics on the other's learning process. To address this challenge, we present complementary reinforcement learning paradigms, leveraging model-based and model-free approaches to learn the control policies for the maze and pendulum, respectively. articles.title: RageVLA: Augmentation-Trained Perception and Action for State-of-the-Art Robustness on LIBERO
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23517v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models look saturated on LIBERO, yet most of them fall apart on LIBERO-PRO as soon as an object moves or the instruction asks for something new. We argue that what is missing is not scale but decoupling.
  In these policies, what to do is tied to where things were during training, to the scene around them and to the wording of the instruction. We cut these ties in two places. In the data, LIBERO demonstrations are re-arranged by general rules: every object and fixture is moved and rotated, tasks are carried into other environments and onto other surfaces, and every instruction is paraphrased. In the policy, a perception engine on frozen DINOv3 features, trained on this augmented data, hands the action model the scene in decoupled form: a list of objects with their positions, and a compact code of what the gripper is looking at, next to image and instruction embeddings from TinyCLIP. articles.title: RESCUE Jumper: A Centimeter-Scale Rolling and Jumping Robot for Search and Rescue
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23531v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Centimeter-scale robots are promising for urban search and rescue because they can enter confined spaces that are inaccessible or unsafe for humans. However, their small size limits obstacle traversal after deployment. This paper presents the RESCUE Jumper, a 125 g mobile robot with a 6.2 cm width and 6.2 cm diameter wheels that combines ground rolling with jumping to traverse steps and gaps that exceeds its rolling capability. The RESCUE Jumper uses its two actuators for both rolling mode and jumping by reversing the direction of wheel motion. Forward wheel motion enables rolling, while reverse wheel motion winds a spring steel tail to store elastic potential energy and release it for jumping. The RESCUE Jumper varies tail winding speed to control jump direction, transitioning from backward to forward jumps as winding speed increases from 0.75 rad/s to 8.73 rad/s. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.23563v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many learning-based approaches for deformable linear objects (DLOs) rely on simplified deformation models that neglect dynamic effects and the mechanical response of the objects, limiting their applicability to lightweight, compliant objects and slow motions. Inspired by recent advances in learning physically structured dynamics with coupled oscillator networks (CONs), we propose $\Phi$-CON for learning force-driven DLO dynamics. The model combines a floating-base coupled oscillator network (FBCON), whose latent potential energy depends only on the DLO's shape, with a learned affine diffeomorphism $\Phi$ between observed positions along the DLO and latent coordinates. Its shape dynamics are stable by construction, and its Lagrangian structure yields explicit expressions for kinetic and potential energy.
